docs.title: isoline
docs.text: Financial statement analysis from your terminal, Python, or an AI coding assistant (MCP).

docs.title: What it computes
docs.text:
Engine What it covers Valuation P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA Health Piotroski F-score, Altman Z″, debt/equity, current ratio, interest coverage Growth 3-year revenue and profit CAGR, operating-margin trend, FCF yield Quality DuPont ROE, ROIC, FCF margin, accruals, cash conversion cycle, share dilution Red flags Beneish M-score, negative equity, negative free cash flow, leverage, liquidity Statements Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow for up to four fiscal years, as reported Valuation (DCF) Discounted cash flow with bear/base/bull cases and a sensitivity grid

Every formula is documented in Methodology and checked by hand-computed tests. When the data needed for a metric is missing, isoline shows n/a and says why. It never substitutes zero.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Reports: each scan writes an Excel workbook and a print-ready HTML report laid out like a company's published statements, with a plain-English explanation of every number, strengths and concerns, and a glossary (--no-report to skip). See Reports.
  • Statements: isoline statements AAPL prints the three financial statements; --export saves them as CSV or JSON.
  • Data: Yahoo Finance via yfinance. No API key needed. It is an unofficial source: coverage varies by company and exchange, and values can be delayed or wrong.
  • Python SDK and MCP server (optional extra) on the same engine.
  • Local: runs on your machine; isoline sends no telemetry.

docs.title: The summary
docs.text:
Each scan includes a short, rule-based text summary built from the numbers (no generative model), for example:

Strong fundamentals (Piotroski F-score of 8). Financially safe (Altman Z-score of 4.65). Operating margins are improving. No red flags were triggered by the checks that could be run.

It describes the data; it is not a recommendation.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install isoline
isoline scan AAPL
isoline scan INFY.NS

See the Quickstart, CLI, SDK and MCP pages.

Isoline provides screening statistics from public data. It is not investment advice and is not a SEBI-registered research analyst or investment adviser.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The README download badge showed only the last 30 days (979) because no pepy.tech API key is set. It now shows all-time downloads of isoline and the legacy telmus combined as one number (16.7k at the time of writing), read from pepy.tech's public badge when no key is set. If a count cannot be read, the previous badge stays instead of a partial or estimated figure.
  • Each nightly badge update also triggered a failed Vercel preview, because the badges branch holds only the badge data and has no website/ folder. The branch now carries a Vercel config that skips deployment.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Financial statements in every scan: income statement, balance sheet and cash flow for up to four fiscal years, newest first, as reported (isoline statements TICKER, with --json and --export .csv/.json; SDK isoline.sdk.statements(); MCP tool statements). Values are matched to fiscal periods by date and never estimated; free cash flow and total liabilities and equity are marked when computed; a balance check warns when the source data does not balance. Capex, dividends and buybacks are always shown as outflows whatever sign the provider uses.
  • HTML report redesigned after real documents. The statements follow published annual reports (for example a US 10-K): one plain typeface, black type, a unit line such as "(In millions of USD, except per-share amounts)", group labels with indented items, a currency sign on the first row and totals, single rules above subtotals and double rules under totals, negatives in parentheses, plus change-vs-prior-year and common-size columns. The rest follows equity research reports: a key-data block (revenue, profit, free cash flow, scores, DCF fair value), Strengths and Concerns, then the detail. Written for beginners too: a "How to read this report" box, a "What it shows" line for each statement, a plain-English "What it means" sentence for every measure using the company's own numbers, and a glossary. Includes a discounted-cash-flow section (assumptions explained, three cases, sensitivity grid, or why it could not be calculated); prints to A4 with page numbers.
  • Comparison report gains key financials side by side (with a warning when currencies differ) and both default DCF values; the screen report states its criteria.
  • Portfolio report (from isoline powerbi) rebuilt as a self-contained report; it replaces the old dashboard that loaded an unpinned Chart.js from a CDN.
  • Excel workbooks gain Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow sheets.
  • MCP tool value (DCF with validated, bounded inputs) and SDK isoline.sdk.value().
  • isoline screen --no-report/--no-open.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Spreadsheet formula injection is neutralised in every CSV and .xlsx written (OWASP "CSV injection"): text from data providers can no longer become a live formula.
  • One validator for tickers, sectors and numeric options across the CLI, terminal interface, SDK and MCP server; MCP arguments are type- and range-checked before anything is fetched. Index symbols such as ^GSPC are now accepted, as documented.
  • HTML reports carry a Content-Security-Policy that forbids scripts and remote loads; the website carries one that allows only its own inline scripts by hash (checked by a test).
  • The Excel exporter no longer downloads data during export (it re-fetched financials and price history); exporters make no network requests.
  • SEC EDGAR requests are restricted to fixed https:// SEC endpoints.
  • CI runs Bandit; a weekly workflow runs pip-audit on the installed dependency tree; Dependabot added; workflows use least-privilege permissions and do not persist the checkout token where nothing is pushed.
  • Unit tests can no longer reach SEC EDGAR by accident (they now make zero network connections).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Website browser-tab icon showed a blank globe: the inline icon contained unescaped quotes that cut the attribute short. The site now ships real favicon.ico, favicon.svg, icon-192.png and an Apple touch icon, generated from the logo.
  • The website's report preview looked doubled (a page inside a page): the sample image included the report's grey screen background, and the frame drew a second sheet. The image is now the report sheet alone, edge to edge, in a single square-cornered frame.
  • Reports show the Isoline mark in their header and as their browser-tab icon (base64-embedded, kept identical to the brand files by a test).
  • isoline serve printed a configuration snippet to standard output before starting, corrupting the MCP stdio channel (clients logged "Failed to parse JSONRPC message"). Standard output now carries only protocol messages; the hint goes to standard error, and only in a terminal.
  • The MCP server works with both MCP Python SDK 1.x and 2.x (2.x replaced the decorator API with constructor handlers); the mcp extra now allows <3, and CI tests the 1.x path in a separate job. Verified with real stdio sessions on both SDKs.
  • A test that timed two concurrent scans with a stopwatch failed on slow CI runners; it now proves concurrency with a barrier.
  • A ticker that fails in isoline powerbi is skipped and reported instead of aborting the whole export.
  • Reports open in the browser by absolute file URI, and a missing browser never fails the command.
  • Red flags read in plain English in summaries and reports ("negative free cash flow in 2+ years").

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Brand: black, white and one vermilion signal colour, replacing navy and amber. The mark is nested contour lines (isolines) around a summit point; the "isoline" wordmark has a vermilion dot on the "i". Light and dark wordmarks and an SVG favicon are generated by examples/make_brand_assets.py, with text converted to outlines so they render the same on GitHub, PyPI and the docs.
  • Website (now at https://isolinee.vercel.app) rebuilt with scroll-driven scenes that use the real engine output for the synthetic sample company: statements loading, the nine Piotroski signals ticking, the Altman Z″ gauge, withheld metrics, a DCF that projects, discounts and stress-tests, and the report scrolling in a browser frame. Interactive ridgeline terrain in the hero, light and dark themes, no third-party scripts. With reduced motion or without JavaScript the page shows every final state as ordinary sections.
  • HTML report and terminal interface use the same neutral palette. Status colours (good, warning, bad) keep their meaning.
  • Demo GIF and social preview redone in the new brand (examples/make_demo_gif.py also writes docs/assets/og.png). examples/make_sample_assets.py now renders sample-report.png itself.
  • Project homepage in the package metadata, the README and the docs header now point to https://isolinee.vercel.app.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• docs/changelog.md is in sync with this file again (CI failed on the previous merge because it wasn't).
  • Type checking no longer breaks with numpy 2.5 or newer, whose stubs use Python 3.12 syntax that mypy rejects when targeting 3.10.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • isoline tui: full-screen terminal interface (optional extra: pip install "isoline[tui]", built on Textual). Four distinct workflows (Fundamental, Valuation, Compare, Screening), a command palette (Ctrl+K), session history, keyboard shortcuts, loading and error states. Work runs in a background thread. Tested headlessly with Textual's pilot.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The compare and screen table printers are now shared functions used by both the command line and the terminal interface.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • isoline value TICKER: discounted-cash-flow estimate (free cash flow to equity, Gordon-growth terminal value, growth fading to terminal) with bear/base/bull scenarios, a discount-rate x terminal-growth sensitivity grid, margin of safety and a --json mode. All assumptions are printed; defaults are labelled; nothing is computed from a non-positive cash flow. Documented on the new Valuation page with sources; the arithmetic is covered by hand-checked tests.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Logo redrawn as a plain geometric mark: a lowercase "i" whose dot sits on a level line (an isoline). The earlier wave motif looked generic.
  • README now shows a wide animated demo (terminal scan, then the report) instead of two tall screenshots. examples/make_demo_gif.py regenerates it from the real engines and a labelled synthetic company.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • PyPI and GitHub page. New README with logo, real terminal and report images (rendered from a labelled synthetic company by examples/make_sample_assets.py), and a "formerly Telmus" notice.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Report charts: the value axis stopped at the last tick below the data, so the tallest bars could extend past the top of the chart. The axis now always covers the largest value. Test added.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Renamed from Telmus to Isoline. New PyPI project isoline, command isoline, import isoline. Behaviour and formulas are unchanged. Environment variables are now ISOLINE_*; the old TELMUS_* names still work. The earlier telmus releases stay on PyPI; a final telmus release (see legacy/telmus-shim) installs isoline and keeps the old command and import working with a deprecation notice. Download counts of telmus do not transfer to isoline.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• SEC EDGAR fallback. When Yahoo Finance is rate-limited, unreachable or has no statements for a US ticker, Telmus now reads the official annual XBRL facts from SEC EDGAR (free, no key, polite rate limiting, declared User-Agent via TELMUS_CONTACT). Results are labelled with their source in the notes; there is no live price from this source, so valuation multiples are n/a. Non-US tickers do not fall back. TELMUS_NO_FALLBACK=1 disables it. Tested offline against a fixture; not yet verified live.
  • Data sources page rewritten with researched limits of the other free APIs (FMP, Alpha Vantage, Finnhub) and why they are not bundled.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• telmus compare crashed with ValueError: I/O operation on closed file. The two tickers are scanned concurrently and each scan silenced provider output with contextlib.redirect_stdout, which is process-wide; overlapping scans restored each other's streams in the wrong order and left sys.stdout closed. Output is now silenced by a ref-counted guard that restores the original streams exactly once. Regression test added.
  • compare: the terminal table, CSV export and HTML report now share one definition (telmus/core/comparison.py). Valuation multiples are shown but never ranked; a missing value never wins; a real 0 is kept in CSV (only missing values are empty).
  • The hidden comp alias now accepts --export/--report/--no-report/--open/--no-open; company names with spaces produce valid file names; scan --json prints raw JSON (no wrapping or markup).
  • New end-to-end test file covering every command with a mocked provider.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Repository layout. The root now holds only standard files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY, pyproject, mkdocs.yml). Project docs moved to docs/project/ (architecture, data sources, release process, roadmap, growth plan) and internal notes to docs/internal/ (kept out of the published site). The Streamlit app moved from dashboard/ to examples/. Removed scripts/capture.py (a one-off screenshot helper with hard-coded personal paths) and an unused logo file. .gitignore reorganised and now ignores .pypirc.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Report fonts and charts. Headings use Times New Roman and numbers use a lining, tabular sans-serif (Georgia's old-style digits made figures look uneven). Scan reports now include two inline-SVG charts built from up to four fiscal years of real statement data, matched by date: revenue and net income with operating margin, and net income vs operating cash flow vs free cash flow. A year that was not reported has no bar (never a zero bar). New history field in the JSON output.
  • Docs site. New Reports page; Architecture, Data sources, Release process, Roadmap and Changelog are now published in the docs navigation (a test keeps the root files and their docs copies identical and checks that every page is in the nav). The docs workflow builds with --strict before deploying.
  • Website and README text updated to describe the report accurately (no more "interactive dashboard with gauges, radar charts"; no CDN claim).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Reports rebuilt. The HTML scan, compare and screen reports are now formal, print-ready documents: light layout, serif headings, tables with "what it measures" columns, status words (Strong / Adequate / Weak / n/a) instead of colour alone, a Piotroski signal table, notes explaining every n/a, and a disclaimer. They are fully self-contained (no JavaScript, no Chart.js CDN, no web fonts, no logo lookups), so they look the same offline and print cleanly. This also fixes the misaligned, differently sized gauges.
  • Speed. Statements are fetched concurrently (about the slowest request instead of the sum of four); compare scans both tickers at the same time; the unused fast_info request and the per-report logo lookup (an extra network call) are gone.

docs.title: Fixed (reports, docs, screening: found in a second, deeper audit)
docs.text:
• HTML report showed missing data as 0 (P/E 0.0, "HEALTH: WEAK", "GROWTH: DECLINING", "VALUATION: FAIR", "Beneish 0.00 = low manipulation risk") and unavailable Piotroski signals as failures. It now shows n/a, "N/A" badges and neutral signal markers. The header said v0.2.6 and the footer printed a literal {telmus_version}; both now show the real version.
  • Excel report header said v0.1.0, used the old Altman thresholds (2.99/1.81) and showed "ok" for n/a rows; now correct, with the n/a reasons listed on the Summary sheet.
  • Power BI radar scored a missing leverage as a perfect 10 and other gaps as 0; gaps are now blank.
  • screen: an unknown sector silently screened IT; now exit code 2 with the valid sectors. Tickers that fail are reported as skipped with the reason instead of vanishing. The MCP screen tool scanned bare symbols (US listings) instead of NSE tickers; it now shares the CLI's universe.
  • MCP scan_ticker ignored its exchange argument; it now applies it (INFY + NSE = INFY.NS).
  • CLI: telmus check printed "n/a" for a legitimate score of 0; percentages now display as percentages; n/a rows show an n/a status, not "ok".
  • Summary text no longer says "Suitable for DCF or comparable company analysis" (that read as a recommendation) and has correct capitalisation; "AI Analyst Brief" renamed "Summary (rule-based)" because it is not AI.
  • Website showed real companies (INFY, AAPL, RELIANCE, MSFT) with numbers from the pre-fix formulas; replaced with clearly labelled synthetic samples. Removed the unverifiable "50,000+ tickers" claim and the wrong "Python 3.9+".

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• from telmus import scan, compare, TelmusScanner, ScanResult now works as documented (lazy import). telmus.sdk exports the error classes.
  • Docs rewritten from the actual behaviour: SDK, CLI, MCP (stdio, not a port), Quickstart, homepage. They previously described methods and options that did not exist and showed invented example numbers.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Quality metrics (ScanResult.quality, CLI "Quality" table, HTML report section): DuPont ROE decomposition, ROIC, free-cash-flow margin and FCF/net income, accruals ratio, DSO/DIO/DPO, cash conversion cycle, share-count change. Formulas in docs/methodology.md; missing inputs give n/a with a note.
  • Release safeguards: RELEASES_DISABLED kill switch, PyPI version-conflict check, post-release smoke test (see Release process).
  • Project docs: ROADMAP, ARCHITECTURE, DATA_SOURCES, RELEASE_PROCESS, BUSINESS_STRATEGY, COMPETITOR_RESEARCH, PROJECT_STATUS.

docs.title: v0.3.2
docs.text: First published release containing everything below (tags v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 were created but never published; the release workflow now supports PyPI Trusted Publishing).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Install: pip install telmus produced a CLI that crashed on every command when pip picked mcp 2.x. mcp is now an optional extra (pip install "telmus[mcp]", pinned <2); the CLI no longer imports it unless you run telmus serve.
  • Beneish M-score was not Beneish's model (DSRI was a gross-margin ratio, LVGI used interest expense, TATA had the wrong sign and denominator) and returned nothing on current yfinance data. Rewritten per the paper, with hand-computed tests. Reported M-scores change.
  • Altman Z″ now uses book equity / total liabilities as in the paper (was market cap), and no longer falls back to total equity or zero when retained earnings are missing. Reported Z-scores change.
  • Piotroski F-score follows the paper (beginning-of-year assets, long-term debt / average assets, share count instead of par value). A missing signal now withholds the score instead of counting as a fail. Reported F-scores change.
  • yfinance row names: both legacy and current labels are supported (previously Beneish and D/E silently returned nothing).
  • Free-cash-flow flag mis-added capex when yfinance reports it as a negative number.
  • Valuation: Series or Series crash when a "Cash" row existed; invented peer comparison removed (vs_sector is now n/a).
  • HTML reports escape company names and other third-party text.
  • Interest coverage no longer substitutes EBITDA for EBIT; negative equity no longer yields a negative debt/equity.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• telmus --version, --debug; scan/compare accept --no-report and --no-open.
  • Friendly errors with hints and exit codes (0 ok, 1 no data/error, 2 usage, 3 network); no tracebacks unless --debug.
  • Ticker validation; automatic retry with backoff for network and rate-limit errors.
  • notes in scan results explaining every n/a; disclaimer in CLI output.
  • 40+ new tests (hand-computed formulas, errors, retries, escaping); tests run offline.
  • CI on Windows, macOS and Linux for Python 3.10-3.13, with clean-wheel install checks; release workflow checks tag == version.
  • docs/methodology.md, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, issue and PR templates.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Minimum Python is 3.10 (the previous 3.9 claim was untrue: mcp needs 3.10).
  • Version has a single source: telmus/__init__.py.
  • Removed one-off scripts from scripts/ and a scratch network script from tests/.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
isoline [--version] [--debug] COMMAND [ARGS]

--debug (or ISOLINE_DEBUG=1) shows full tracebacks. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 no data / other error, 2 bad input (ticker, sector), 3 network or provider unavailable.

Tickers use Yahoo Finance format: AAPL, INFY.NS (NSE), 500209.BO (BSE), VOD.L (London).

docs.title: scan
docs.text:
isoline scan AAPL
isoline scan INFY.NS --export infy.xlsx        # .xlsx, .csv or .json
isoline scan AAPL --json                        # raw JSON to the terminal
isoline scan AAPL --no-report --no-open         # terminal only, write nothing

Prints Valuation, Health, Growth and Quality tables, a rule-based summary and a note for every metric that is n/a. By default it also writes <TICKER>_analysis.xlsx and <TICKER>_dashboard.html to the current folder and opens the HTML in your browser; --no-report / --no-open turn that off.

docs.title: compare
docs.text: isoline compare AAPL MSFT [--export out.xlsx|.csv|.json] [--no-report] [--no-open]

docs.title: value
docs.text:
isoline value AAPL --discount 0.09 --growth 0.07
isoline value MSFT --json

DCF estimate with scenarios and a sensitivity grid. See Valuation for the method and assumptions.

docs.title: statements
docs.text:
isoline statements AAPL
isoline statements INFY.NS --export infy_statements.csv
isoline statements MSFT --json

The income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement for up to four fiscal years, newest first, as reported. Amounts are shown in one unit (for example USD millions) with costs and outflows in parentheses. Lines a company did not report show n/a; free cash flow and total liabilities and equity are marked * when they are computed from reported lines. If the balance sheet does not balance in some year, a warning says so. --export writes .csv or .json.

docs.title: screen
docs.text:
isoline screen IT --min-piotroski 6 --max-de 1.0
isoline screen Banking --export banks.csv

Options: --export FILE, --no-report (write no Excel/HTML), --no-open (do not open the report). --min-piotroski must be 0 to 9 and --max-de 0 to 1000.

Screens a small built-in example list (sectors IT and Banking, five NSE tickers each), not the whole market. Tickers whose data cannot be fetched or scored are listed as skipped with the reason. Banks are usually skipped because Piotroski and debt/equity are not meaningful for them. An unknown sector exits with code 2 and lists the valid ones.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
isoline check AAPL

Prints just the Piotroski F-score and Altman Z″ (and notes), no files.

docs.title: powerbi
docs.text:
isoline powerbi INFY.NS TCS.NS --export portfolio.csv
isoline powerbi --tickers INFY.NS TCS.NS --export flags.csv --flags

Writes the CSV plus a *_report.html portfolio report (one row per company, averages of reported values, and a summary per company). A ticker that cannot be loaded is skipped and listed, instead of aborting the export; the command fails only if no ticker could be analysed.

docs.title: tui
docs.text:
pip install "isoline[tui]"
isoline tui

Opens the full-screen terminal interface: four modes (scan, valuation, compare, screen), a command palette on Ctrl+K and session history. See Terminal interface.

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
pip install "isoline[mcp]"
isoline serve

Starts the MCP server over stdio. See MCP.

docs.title: info
docs.text: Prints version, Python version, data source and coverage.

docs.title: MCP Server Guide
docs.text: isoline can run as an MCP server so AI assistants and agents can call financial analytics tools directly. This makes valuation, health, growth, and red-flag metrics available to Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP-compatible clients.

docs.title: Why use isoline as an MCP server
docs.text:
• Get deterministic, documented financial metrics instead of model-generated numbers.
  • Let AI agents fetch company analysis automatically during conversations.
  • Keep your local environment in control while giving assistants structured access to tools.
  • Same engine as the CLI and the Python SDK.

docs.title: Install and start
docs.text:
pip install "isoline[mcp]"
isoline serve

isoline serve speaks MCP over stdio: it opens no network port and writes nothing to standard output except protocol messages (run by hand in a terminal, it shows a setup hint on standard error). It works with the MCP Python SDK 1.x and 2.x. You normally don't run it by hand; your MCP client launches it (see the client examples below). Without the extra installed, the command exits with a message telling you to install it.

docs.title: Available MCP tools
docs.text:
Tool Inputs Returns scan ticker {"result": ScanResult} (same JSON as scan(...).to_dict()) scan_ticker ticker, optional exchange (NSE, BSE, LSE, NYSE, NASDAQ, US) same; INFY + NSE scans INFY.NS; a ticker that already has a suffix is left alone; unknown exchange is an error compare ticker_a, ticker_b {"result": CompareResult} screen optional sector (IT or Banking, default IT), min_piotroski (default 0), max_de (default 10) {"matches": [ScanResult...], "skipped": {ticker: reason}}; unknown sector is an error statements ticker {"ticker", "statements": {periods, currency, income, balance, cashflow, notes}}; values as reported, sign -1 marks a cost value ticker, optional discount (0-1), growth (-0.5-1), terminal (-0.05-0.2), years (1-15) {"result": DCFResult} with every assumption, scenarios and the sensitivity grid info none {version, data_source, coverage, description}

Every argument is validated before anything is fetched: tickers must look like tickers (no paths, markup or control characters) and numbers must be finite and within the stated ranges. Invalid input is returned as an error, never passed to a data provider.

Missing metrics are null with an explanation in each result's notes. screen only covers the small built-in example lists described in the CLI page.

docs.text:
Ask the assistant to:

  • Analyze INFY financials

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• isoline serve prints "needs the optional mcp extra": run pip install "isoline[mcp]".
  • The client cannot start the server: make sure isoline is on the PATH of the app that launches it (on Windows/macOS GUI apps this can differ from your terminal; use the full path to isoline in command).
  • A ticker is not found: add the exchange suffix (INFY.NS) or pass exchange to scan_ticker.
  • Data is from Yahoo Finance (unofficial). Output is screening statistics, not investment advice.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
Isoline reads annual statements from Yahoo Finance and reports screening statistics, not investment advice. Rules that apply everywhere:

  • A missing input gives n/a, never 0. A genuine zero stays zero.
  • A score is shown only when every input it needs exists for the required years.
  • Statement rows are looked up by canonical name, so both old and current yfinance labels work.
  • Year t is the latest fiscal year, t-1 the one before.

docs.title: Piotroski F-score (0-9)
docs.text:
Piotroski (2000), Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers, Journal of Accounting Research 38. One point per signal:

Signal Passes when ROA positive Net income(t) / total assets(t-1) > 0 CFO positive Operating cash flow(t) > 0 ROA improving ROA(t) > ROA(t-1), each over beginning-of-year assets Low accruals Operating cash flow(t) > net income(t) Leverage falling Long-term debt / average total assets lower than last year Liquidity rising Current ratio(t) > current ratio(t-1) No dilution Shares outstanding(t) <= shares outstanding(t-1) Gross margin rising Gross margin(t) > gross margin(t-1) Asset turnover rising Revenue(t) / total assets(t-1) > same for t-1

Needs three balance-sheet years. If any signal cannot be computed the score is withheld and the missing signals are listed. Designed for value stocks; interpret with care elsewhere.

docs.title: Altman Z″-score
docs.text:
Altman (1983/1995) model for non-manufacturers and emerging markets:

Z″ = 6.56·X1 + 3.26·X2 + 6.72·X3 + 1.05·X4

X1 = working capital / total assets, X2 = retained earnings / total assets, X3 = EBIT / total assets, X4 = book equity / total liabilities. Zones: above 2.6 safe, 1.1-2.6 grey, below 1.1 distress. Not computed for financial firms.

docs.title: Beneish M-score
docs.text:
Beneish (1999), The Detection of Earnings Manipulation, Financial Analysts Journal 55(5).

M = -4.84 + 0.920·DSRI + 0.528·GMI + 0.404·AQI + 0.892·SGI + 0.115·DEPI - 0.172·SGAI + 4.679·TATA - 0.327·LVGI

Index Definition DSRI (Receivables/Sales)(t) ÷ (Receivables/Sales)(t-1) GMI Gross margin(t-1) ÷ gross margin(t) AQI 1 - (current assets + net PP&E)/total assets ÷ same(t-1) SGI Sales(t) ÷ Sales(t-1) DEPI Dep/(Dep + net PP&E) ÷ same(t) SGAI (SG&A/Sales)(t) ÷ (SG&A/Sales)(t-1) LVGI (current liabilities + long-term debt)/total assets ÷ same(t-1) TATA (Net income - operating cash flow) / total assets(t)

TATA uses the cash-flow form of total accruals. A score above -2.22 raises a high-severity flag (Beneish's paper also discusses -1.78, which flags fewer companies). Not computed for financial firms.

docs.title: Ratios and flags
docs.text:
• Debt / equity is total liabilities / shareholders' equity. Not reported when equity <= 0; negative equity raises its own high-severity flag.
  • Interest coverage = EBIT / |interest expense|. EBITDA is never substituted for EBIT.
  • Negative FCF flag: free cash flow (operating cash flow minus |capex|) negative in 2+ of the last 3 years.
  • Liabilities/equity > 2 raises a medium flag.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: Annual data only; no restatement tracking; no currency conversion (ratios are unit-free, absolute values are in the reporting currency); fiscal years are not calendar-aligned across companies; sector peer valuation is not implemented; data quality is bounded by Yahoo Finance.

docs.title: Quality metrics (v0.3.3, isoline/core/engines/quality.py)
docs.text:
All flow items are for the latest fiscal year; return denominators use the average of year-end and prior year-end balances. Missing inputs give n/a plus a note, never zero, and no tax rate is assumed.

Metric Formula Net margin Net income / Revenue Asset turnover Revenue / Average total assets Equity multiplier Average total assets / Average equity ROE (DuPont) Net margin x Asset turnover x Equity multiplier = Net income / Average equity (n/a if average equity <= 0) ROIC EBIT x (1 - effective tax rate) / Average invested capital, where invested capital = equity + total debt - cash and effective tax rate = tax provision / pretax income (n/a for financials or if the tax rate is unavailable) FCF Operating cash flow - abs(capex); FCF margin = FCF / Revenue; FCF / Net income only when net income > 0 Accruals ratio (Net income - Operating cash flow) / Average total assets (Sloan, 1996) DSO / DIO / DPO Receivables x 365 / Revenue; Inventory x 365 / COGS; Payables x 365 / COGS (year-end balances) Cash conversion cycle DSO + DIO - DPO; n/a unless all three are computable (n/a for financials) Share count change (Shares t - Shares t-1) / Shares t-1

Verification: every row is covered by a hand-computed test in tests/test_scores.py, including the DuPont identity. Not yet verified against live provider data.

docs.title: Power BI Integration Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to use isoline to generate datasets optimized for Microsoft Power BI, import them, construct interactive financial dashboards, and automate data refreshes to monitor stock metrics over time.

docs.title: 1. What is Power BI Desktop?
docs.text:
Power BI Desktop is a free, professional data visualization and business intelligence application developed by Microsoft. It allows you to connect to multiple data sources, clean and transform data, and build highly interactive reports with drag-and-drop visuals.

  • Download Link: You can download it for free directly from the Microsoft Store or from the official Power BI download page.

docs.title: 2. Generating the Power BI CSV Files
docs.text: Use isoline to export fundamental stock data. isoline outputs null values as empty fields ("") rather than placeholder strings (like "n/a"), allowing Power BI to automatically parse them as numeric types (Decimal, Integer) rather than Text.

docs.title: Standard Portfolio Export
docs.text:
Run this command to export general valuation, health, and growth metrics:

isoline powerbi --tickers INFY.NS TCS.NS WIPRO.NS HDFCBANK.NS RELIANCE.NS --export portfolio.csv

docs.title: Red Flags Export (Granular tracking)
docs.text:
Run this command to export flag-level details for each ticker (one row per flag per ticker):

isoline powerbi --tickers INFY.NS TCS.NS WIPRO.NS --flags --export flags.csv

docs.title: 3. Importing Data into Power BI
docs.text:
1. Open Power BI Desktop.
  2. On the Home ribbon, click on Get Data and select Text/CSV.
  3. Choose your exported portfolio.csv (or flags.csv) and click Open.
  4. In the preview window, confirm that columns are formatted properly.
  5. Click Load (or click Transform Data if you wish to adjust columns, rename fields, or merge sources in the Power Query editor first).

docs.title: 4. Building the Visuals
docs.text: Construct a premium financial dashboard using these six visuals:

docs.title: 1. Bar Chart: Piotroski F-Score by Company
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Clustered Bar Chart or Clustered Column Chart.
  • Configuration:
  • Y-Axis / X-Axis (Categories): Drag the Ticker field.
  • X-Axis / Y-Axis (Values): Drag Piotroski_F and set it to Average (or Sum).
  • Styling: Turn on Data Labels and set the bar fill color to a deep steel blue.
  • What it looks like: A clean horizontal bar chart showing each stock on the y-axis, with its corresponding Piotroski score represented by a colored bar extending to the right (scores range from 0 to 9).

docs.title: 2. Scatter Plot: P/E Ratio vs. Revenue CAGR
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Scatter Chart.
  • Configuration:
  • X-Axis: Drag PE_Ratio (Average).
  • Y-Axis: Drag Revenue_CAGR_3Y (Average).
  • Values: Drag Ticker.
  • Size (Bubble size): Drag PE_Ratio or another volume metric (like Piotroski score) to represent valuation size.
  • What it looks like: A 2D quadrant bubble chart. Strong growth/cheap value stocks will sit in the upper-left quadrant (low P/E, high growth), while expensive/low-growth stocks sit in the bottom-right.

docs.title: 3. Card Visuals: Core Health KPIs
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Card (or Multi-row card).
  • Visual 1:
  • Field: Drag Piotroski_F and set to Average.
  • Label: Rename to "Avg Piotroski F-Score".
  • Visual 2:
  • Field: Drag Altman_Z and set to Average.
  • Label: Rename to "Avg Altman Z-Score".
  • What it looks like: Large, clean callout cards showing the average scores across your entire portfolio (e.g., a big bold 5.45 and 4.82).

docs.title: 4. Table: Portfolio Summary & Conditional Formatting
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Table.
  • Configuration:
  • Add columns: Ticker, Company, PE_Ratio, Piotroski_F, Altman_Z, Highest_Concern, Analyst_Brief.
  • Conditional Formatting:
  • Right-click Highest_Concern (or the Ticker cell) in the Visualizations pane, go to Conditional formatting > Background color.
  • Set Rules based on the Highest_Concern field:
    • If value is high -> Soft Red background (#F8D7DA)
    • If value is medium -> Soft Orange background (#FFF3CD)
    • If value is low -> Soft Green background (#D4EDDA)
  • What it looks like: A tabular grid with all company metrics. Cells under the concern or ticker column will be highlighted in green, yellow, or red based on their financial risk.

docs.title: 5. Donut Chart: Risk Level Distribution
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Donut Chart.
  • Configuration:
  • Legend: Drag Highest_Concern.
  • Values: Drag Ticker (Count or Count Distinct).
  • Styling: Map green to low, orange to medium, and red to high.
  • What it looks like: A segmented circle showing the percentage of your portfolio in each risk category.

docs.title: 6. Line Chart: Track Scores Over Time
docs.text:
• Visual Type: Line Chart.
  • Configuration:
  • X-Axis: Drag Date.
  • Y-Axis: Drag Piotroski_F (Average) or Altman_Z (Average).
  • Legend: Drag Ticker.
  • What it looks like: A multi-line chart with dates on the horizontal axis and scores on the vertical axis, mapping the score changes of each company week-over-week.

docs.title: 5. Setting Up Auto-Refreshes & Historical Tracking
docs.text: To track historical trends in Power BI, you must append weekly/monthly runs to the same dataset.

docs.title: Step 1: Scripting the Append
docs.text:
Instead of overwriting the CSV, write a script that runs isoline and appends rows to your portfolio master CSV:

# PowerShell script (e.g., update_portfolio.ps1)
# Fetch standard metrics for this week and append to master database
isoline powerbi --tickers INFY.NS TCS.NS WIPRO.NS --export temp_week.csv

# If master.csv doesn't exist, create it with headers, otherwise skip headers and append
if (-Not (Test-Path master.csv)) {
    Copy-Item temp_week.csv master.csv
} else {
    # Skip the header row (first line) and append the data to master.csv
    Get-Content temp_week.csv | Select-Object -Skip 1 | Add-Content master.csv
}
Remove-Item temp_week.csv

docs.title: Step 2: Task Scheduling
docs.text: Schedule this script to run weekly using Windows Task Scheduler: 1. Open Task Scheduler and click Create Basic Task. 2. Set Trigger to Weekly (e.g., every Sunday at 6 PM). 3. Set Action to Start a program. 4. Program: powershell.exe 5. Arguments: -File C:\path\to\update_portfolio.ps1

docs.title: Step 3: Refreshing Power BI
docs.text: Inside Power BI Desktop, clicking the Refresh button on the Home ribbon will reload master.csv, pulling in the new weekly data points. The line charts will automatically draw the new historical trends based on the Date column!

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Python 3.10 or newer.

pip install isoline
isoline --version

Use a virtual environment (python -m venv .venv) and avoid creating it inside a cloud-synced folder such as OneDrive, which can corrupt installs on Windows.

docs.title: 2. Scan a stock
docs.text:
isoline scan AAPL          # US
isoline scan INFY.NS       # NSE (India); BSE uses .BO

Tickers use Yahoo Finance symbols. Non-US stocks need the exchange suffix.

The output has Valuation, Health, Growth and Quality tables, a rule-based summary, and a line for every metric that could not be computed. This is real output on a synthetic company with deliberately incomplete data (not a real stock):

Valuation   P/E ratio 25.00 | P/B ratio 5.00 | EV/EBITDA n/a
Health      Piotroski F-score 8 | Altman Z-score 4.65 | Debt/Equity 0.83 | Current ratio 2.00
Growth      Revenue CAGR 3y n/a | Margin trend improving | FCF yield 3.0%
Quality     ROE (DuPont) 21.4% | Net margin 12.0% | ROIC n/a | Cash conversion (days) n/a

Note: ROIC not reported: effective tax rate unavailable (no rate is assumed).

By default a scan also writes <TICKER>_analysis.xlsx and <TICKER>_dashboard.html in the current folder and opens the HTML. Use --no-report --no-open for terminal-only output.

docs.title: 3. Reading the scores
docs.text:
Metric How to read it Piotroski F (0-9) 8-9 strong, 5-7 average, 0-4 weak. Only reported when all nine signals are computable. Altman Z″ above 2.6 safe, 1.1-2.6 grey zone, below 1.1 distress. Not applicable to banks and insurers. Beneish M (8-variable) above -2.22 suggests possible earnings manipulation. Not applicable to financial firms. FCF yield (operating cash flow minus capex) / market cap ROIC EBIT x (1 - effective tax rate) / average invested capital Cash conversion cycle DSO + DIO - DPO, in days

Exact definitions: Methodology. A flagged score is a prompt to look closer, not a verdict.

docs.title: 4. JSON and exports
docs.text:
isoline scan AAPL --json
isoline scan AAPL --export aapl.json      # .json, .csv or .xlsx

docs.title: 5. Compare two stocks
docs.text: isoline compare AAPL MSFT

docs.title: 6. Read the financial statements
docs.text:
isoline statements AAPL
isoline statements AAPL --export aapl_statements.csv

docs.title: 7. Files written
docs.text:
Command Files scan T T_analysis.xlsx, T_dashboard.html compare A B AvsB_comparison.xlsx, AvsB_dashboard.html screen IT screen_results.xlsx, screen_dashboard.html; --export adds .xlsx/.csv/.json powerbi ... --export p.csv p.csv, p_report.html statements T --export f f (.csv or .json)

Add --no-report to scan, compare or screen to write no files, and --no-open to keep the browser closed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Could not reach Yahoo Finance: check your connection or proxy, and retry in a minute (Yahoo rate-limits).
  • No data: check the symbol and exchange suffix on finance.yahoo.com.
  • Add --debug to any command for the full traceback when reporting an issue.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: isoline scan, compare and screen write an HTML report and an Excel workbook; isoline powerbi writes a CSV and a portfolio report. Pass --no-report to write nothing and --no-open to keep the browser closed.

docs.title: HTML report (<TICKER>_dashboard.html)
docs.text:
The layout follows real documents. The statements look like a company's published annual report (for example a US 10-K): one plain typeface, black type, fiscal years in columns with the newest first, a unit line such as "(In millions of USD, except per-share amounts)", group labels such as Assets: with indented line items, a currency sign on the first row and on totals, a single rule above subtotals, a double rule under totals and negatives in parentheses. The rest follows the structure of equity research reports: a key-data block first, then Strengths and Concerns, then the detail.

It is written for first-time readers too: a "How to read this report" box, a "What it shows" line above each statement, a "What it means" sentence next to every measure using the company's own numbers (for example "It has 1.89 of short-term assets for every 1.00 of bills due within a year"), and a glossary.

Section Contents Header and key data Company, ticker, exchange, reporting currency, fiscal years, data source; revenue, net income, free cash flow, Piotroski score, Altman Z″ and the DCF fair value estimate 1 Summary Rule-based summary (not a recommendation), Strengths and Concerns lists built only from computed figures, contents 2 Financial statements Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement for up to four fiscal years, with "change vs prior year" and common-size columns (% of revenue, % of assets) 3 Key measures explained Valuation, financial health, growth, profitability and cash, each with a reading and a plain-English meaning 4 Health scores and red flags The nine Piotroski tests in plain words, Altman Z″, Beneish M, red flags 5 What could the business be worth? Discounted cash flow: base case, every assumption explained, bear/base/bull cases and a sensitivity grid; or why it could not be calculated 6 Trends over time Sales, profit and operating margin; whether profit is turning into cash 7 Notes and sources, 8 Glossary Why each n/a is n/a, method, definitions

It is self-contained: inline styles and inline SVG only, no JavaScript, web fonts, CDN or network requests, and a Content-Security-Policy that forbids them. It opens offline and prints to A4 with page numbers and repeated table headers (use your browser's Print / Save as PDF). Missing data is n/a, never zero; free cash flow and total liabilities and equity are marked † when calculated from reported lines; a balance-sheet check warns when the source data does not balance. Status is always a word, never colour alone. All provider text is HTML-escaped.

compare gives each company's strengths and concerns, key figures side by side (in each company's own currency, with a warning when they differ), a measure-by-measure table with a "Stronger" column only where higher or lower is clearly better, and both DCF values. screen lists the companies that passed with the rules applied. The portfolio report from isoline powerbi lists every company with averages and a company-by-company summary, and names the tickers that could not be analysed.

docs.title: Excel workbook (<TICKER>_analysis.xlsx)
docs.text: Dashboard (with margin and revenue charts built from the scan's own data, so the workbook never needs a second download), Summary, Valuation, Health, Growth and Red Flags sheets, plus Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow sheets at full precision (costs and outflows negative). Missing values are n/a. Text from the data provider can never become a live spreadsheet formula: only Isoline's own sheet references are formulas.

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
pip install isoline

from isoline import scan, compare, IsolineScanner, ScanResult, CompareResult

import isoline is lightweight; the SDK loads on first use. Everything here is tested offline in tests/test_sdk.py. Names not listed on this page are internal and may change.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Call Returns scan(ticker) ScanResult compare(ticker_a, ticker_b) CompareResult (.ticker_a, .ticker_b, .result_a, .result_b) isoline.sdk.compare_to_dataframe(compare_result) pandas.DataFrame indexed by metric, one column per ticker statements(ticker) StatementsResult or None: periods (ISO dates, newest first), currency, income / balance / cashflow as lists of StatementLine(label, values, kind, key, group, sign, per_share, computed), notes value(ticker, discount=None, growth=None, terminal=None, years=5) DCFResult (same as isoline value) IsolineScanner().scan(t) / .compare(a, b) same as above; use when you want one reusable scanner

Tickers use Yahoo Finance format: AAPL, INFY.NS (NSE), 500209.BO (BSE).

docs.title: ScanResult
docs.text:
Field Type Notes ticker, company, exchange str valuation ValuationResult pe_ratio, pb_ratio, ev_ebitda, vs_sector (always None: no peer data), flag health HealthResult piotroski_f (int or None), piotroski_signals (dict of the signals that were computable), altman_z, debt_to_equity, current_ratio, interest_coverage, flag, notes growth GrowthResult revenue_cagr_3y, pat_cagr_3y (fractions, 0.10 = 10%), margin_trend ("improving"/"stable"/"declining"), fcf_yield, flag quality QualityResult DuPont (net_margin, asset_turnover, equity_multiplier, roe), roic, fcf, fcf_margin, fcf_to_net_income, accruals_ratio, dso_days, dio_days, dpo_days, cash_conversion_cycle_days, share_count_change, notes beneish_m float or None flagged as a possible manipulator above -2.22 red_flags list of RedFlag(type, value, severity) highest_concern str "low", "medium" or "high" analyst_brief str rule-based text summary, not advice notes list[str] one line for every metric that is None, saying why statements StatementsResult or None the three statements, as returned by statements(ticker) dcf dict or None default-assumption DCF (DCFResult.to_dict()); when it cannot be computed, assumptions is None and notes say why scan_duration_ms, schema_version int

Missing data is None, never 0. Check result.notes to see why a value is missing (for example, banks have no meaningful Altman Z″ or Beneish M).

Methods: result.to_dict() and result.to_json() (stable shape, schema_version 1).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All inherit IsolineError (a ValueError) and carry a .hint: InvalidTickerError, NoDataError, ProviderUnavailableError, RateLimitError.

from isoline import scan
from isoline.sdk import IsolineError

try:
    r = scan("INFY.NS")
except IsolineError as exc:
    print(exc, "->", exc.hint)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
from isoline import scan

r = scan("AAPL")
print(r.health.piotroski_f, r.health.altman_z, r.quality.roic)
for note in r.notes:
    print("n/a because:", note)

import pandas as pd
from isoline import scan

rows = []
for t in ["INFY.NS", "TCS.NS", "WIPRO.NS"]:
    try:
        r = scan(t)
    except Exception as exc:          # one bad ticker should not stop the loop
        print("skipped", t, exc)
        continue
    rows.append({"ticker": t, "F": r.health.piotroski_f, "Z": r.health.altman_z,
                 "ROIC": r.quality.roic, "CCC days": r.quality.cash_conversion_cycle_days})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows))

import json
from isoline import scan
open("aapl.json", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(scan("AAPL").to_json())

Data comes from Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial, may be delayed or incomplete). Output is screening statistics, not investment advice.

docs.title: Terminal interface
docs.text:
pip install "isoline[tui]"
isoline tui

A full-screen interface over the same engines as the command line. Pick a mode, type, press Enter. Network work runs in the background, so the screen never freezes; a failed lookup shows the reason on screen instead of a traceback.

Mode Key Input Runs Fundamental F2 AAPL or INFY.NS scores, quality, growth, red flags (isoline scan) Valuation F3 AAPL 0.09 0.07 (ticker, discount, growth; the last two optional) DCF with scenarios and sensitivity (isoline value) Compare F4 AAPL MSFT side-by-side comparison (isoline compare) Screening F5 IT or Banking Piotroski and leverage screen (isoline screen)

Each mode runs a different workflow, not a relabelled one. The session list on the left keeps what you ran; select an entry to put it back in the input box.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Action Ctrl+K command palette (search every action) Ctrl+N new analysis (focus the input) F2 to F5 choose mode F1 help Ctrl+L clear output Ctrl+Q quit

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Reports, exports and watchlists stay in the command line for now (--export, --report).
  • The interface is tested headlessly with Textual's test pilot; it has not been exercised on every terminal emulator. If colours look wrong, try Windows Terminal, iTerm2 or a recent GNOME Terminal.

docs.title: Valuation (DCF)
docs.text:
isoline value AAPL --discount 0.09 --growth 0.07 --terminal 0.025 --years 5
isoline value MSFT --json

isoline value estimates the equity value of a company from its own reported cash flow and shows every assumption, three scenarios and a sensitivity grid. It is an illustration of what your assumptions imply. It is not a price target, a recommendation or investment advice.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Step What is done Cash flow Free cash flow = operating cash flow minus the absolute capital expenditure. It is measured after interest, so it approximates free cash flow to equity. Base Mean of up to the last three reported years, to smooth one-off swings. If this is not positive the DCF is not computed (a perpetuity of a negative cash flow has no meaningful value). Growth Year-1 growth (--growth, default: 3-year revenue CAGR limited to 0-15%) fades linearly to terminal growth by the last explicit year. Terminal value Gordon growth: FCF in the last year x (1 + g) / (r - g), discounted back. Requires r > g. Equity value Present value of the explicit cash flows plus the present value of the terminal value. Because the cash flow is already after interest, net debt is not subtracted again. Per share Equity value divided by shares outstanding. Margin of safety (value per share - price) / value per share, only when price and the estimate are in the same currency.

Scenarios: Bear halves growth and adds 1 point to the discount rate; Bull multiplies growth by 1.25 and subtracts 1 point; Base uses your inputs. The grid varies the discount rate by +/-2 points and terminal growth by +/-1 point.

docs.title: Assumptions you must own
docs.text:
• Discount rate. The default of 10% is a placeholder, not an estimate of any company's cost of equity. Set --discount.
  • Terminal growth. Stable growth should not exceed the growth of the economy; the risk-free rate is a common cap (Damodaran). Isoline flags terminal growth above 4%.
  • Terminal weight. When more than 75% of the value comes from the terminal value the output says so.

docs.title: When it returns "not computed"
docs.text: Missing cash-flow items, a non-positive average free cash flow, too little revenue history to derive growth (pass --growth), or a discount rate at or below terminal growth. Data fetched from the SEC fallback has no market price, so the margin of safety is n/a.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Damodaran, Getting Closure in Valuation (terminal value, stable growth cannot exceed the economy's growth): https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pdfiles/valonlineslides/session9.pdf
  • Damodaran, Terminal value notes (risk-free rate as a cap on stable growth): https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pdfiles/country/TerminalValue.pdf

docs.title: Health engine
docs.text: Piotroski F-score, Altman Z″-score, liabilities/equity, current ratio and interest coverage. The exact formulas, references and limits are documented in Methodology.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
isoline/
  cli/app.py          Typer CLI (scan, compare, value, statements, screen, check, powerbi, tui, serve), error mapping, exit codes
  core/
    loaders.py        provider access (yfinance today) with retry/backoff -> dict of DataFrames
    labels.py         canonical line-item aliases; all engines read data only through this
    errors.py         typed errors (+ hint, exit code)
    validation.py     one set of input rules (tickers, sectors, bounded numbers) for CLI, TUI, SDK and MCP
    dcf.py            discounted cash flow, scenarios and sensitivity grid
    engines/          health (F, Z''), flags (Beneish, red flags), growth, valuation, quality, history (chart series),
                      statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow laid out for presentation)
    scanner.py        orchestrates engines -> ScanResult (compare scans both tickers concurrently)
    screening.py      sector screening shared by the CLI and the MCP server
    result.py         dataclasses; to_dict() is the stable JSON shape
  exporters/          report.py (self-contained HTML with a CSP), html_dashboard.py (thin wrapper), excel, powerbi;
                      _safe.py escapes HTML and neutralises spreadsheet formula injection; exporters never use the network
  sdk/                public Python API (scan, compare, statements, value, IsolineScanner)
  mcp/server.py       optional MCP server (extra: isoline[mcp])

Principles: engines are pure functions of data frames (testable offline); provider quirks live only in loaders.py and labels.py; every n/a carries a note; exporters never trust text.

Planned: a DataProvider protocol returning the same frames so SEC EDGAR or CSV sources plug into loaders.py without touching engines (see Data sources).

docs.title: Brand migration plan
docs.text: Status: the owner delegated the choice and Isoline was selected (2026-11-25). The rename is implemented on branch rebrand/isoline (version 0.6.0) and is not merged to main, not published, and no domain is registered. main still ships as telmus. Domain and trademark checks remain open.

docs.title: 1. Name search
docs.text: Thirty-one single words (real words and invented ones) were screened first on PyPI, where each was looked up by exact name on 2026-11-25. Most real words are already taken (for example abacus, meridian, kestrel, vellum, tally, lemma, cairn, anvil, fathom). cadence and isoline were free. A second batch of 40 invented or rarer words was screened the same way; 22 were free, including the finalists below.

docs.title: Shortlist (all verified absent from PyPI on 2026-11-25)
docs.text:
Name Meaning Why it fits Known conflicts found Isoline (recommended) A line joining points of equal value (contour, isobar). Measurement and precision; naturally becomes a logo (parallel lines, a level line). Works as isoline command. 134 GitHub repositories contain the word in their name (e.g. a graphics tool); generic technical term, so search results will be crowded and the trademark is probably weak. No financial-software company found in one web search (inconclusive). Tessarin Invented; echoes tessera (a tile in a mosaic). Distinctive, easy to say, little search noise. 34 GitHub repos with the word in the name. Halden Invented-sounding place name. Short, serious tone. Common surname and place name; one search for conflicts was inconclusive. Altimo Invented; echoes altitude and optimum. Short and neutral. 23 GitHub repos; not researched further. Kelvara Invented. Strong phonetics, unusual. Not researched beyond PyPI.

Eliminated: Vantor, which was free on PyPI but is the new name of a large US spatial-intelligence company (formerly Maxar Intelligence, rebranded Oct 2025). Other names screened out for being taken on PyPI are listed above.

docs.title: What was NOT verified (do not assume these are clear)
docs.text:
• Domains. The sandbox cannot resolve DNS or query registries, so no domain was checked. Check .com/.io/.dev for the finalist at a registrar.
  • Trademarks. USPTO, WIPO and the Indian registry were not searched. Run a search in class 9 and 42 (software) and 36 (financial services) before committing; consider a lawyer.
  • Company conflicts were checked with a single web search per name, which is not a clearance search.

Recommendation: Isoline, subject to domain and trademark checks. If those fail, Tessarin.

docs.title: 2. Preserving the PyPI project and its downloads
docs.text:
Facts that shape the plan:

  • Download counters belong to a project name. They cannot be transferred, merged or renamed, and a new name starts at zero. Do not claim otherwise.
  • PyPI releases cannot be re-uploaded or silently replaced, and project names are not freed by renaming. The existing telmus project stays as it is, with its history.
  • A Trusted Publisher is configured per PyPI project. The new project needs its own "pending publisher" entry before the first release workflow can create it.

Plan:

  1. Keep telmus on PyPI. Never delete it or yank its releases.
  2. After approval, publish the successor as a new project (new name, version 1.0.0 or continuing the series, owner decision) from the same repository history.
  3. Release one final telmus version that is a thin compatibility shim: same CLI entry point, Requires-Dist: <successor>, a one-line deprecation notice on the console and in the description. Existing pip install -U telmus users then receive the successor automatically.
  4. Keep the legacy README and changelog, labelled "superseded by "; the historical download figures stay attributed to telmus.
  5. Keep the Python import telmus working for at least two minor releases through a re-export module that warns once.
  6. Git history is preserved by renaming the package directory with git mv in the same repository (or renaming the repository; GitHub redirects the old URL).

docs.title: 3. Rename checklist (executed only after approval)
docs.text:
The product name lives in telmus/branding.py (display name, package, module, command, tagline, URLs). A rename touches:

  • [ ] telmus/branding.py values
  • [ ] Package directory telmus/ -> new module name (git mv), all from telmus... imports
  • [ ] pyproject.toml: name, [project.scripts], URLs, Trusted Publisher project name
  • [ ] .github/workflows/*: package name in smoke tests and publish steps
  • [ ] README.md, docs/**, mkdocs.yml (site name, repo, URLs), website/index.html
  • [ ] MCP server name and docs/mcp.md config snippet
  • [ ] Report footers, disclaimers, Excel/Power BI titles (read from BRAND)
  • [ ] Environment variables (TELMUS_CONTACT, TELMUS_NO_FALLBACK): accept old and new names
  • [ ] GitHub repository rename (owner action), Vercel project and domain (owner action)
  • [ ] PyPI: create pending publisher, publish successor, then publish the telmus shim
  • [ ] CHANGELOG.md migration entry; keep old entries unchanged

A test (tests/test_branding.py) already checks that BRAND matches pyproject.toml.

docs.title: 4. Approval gates
docs.text: Not done without explicit approval: registering any domain, publishing any package under a new name, renaming the GitHub repository, changing PyPI ownership, spending money.

docs.title: Data sources
docs.text:
No free source is complete, accurate, real-time and worldwide at once. Isoline therefore layers sources, says which one produced each result, and shows n/a rather than guessing.

Source Status Coverage Limits (researched Nov 2026) Yahoo Finance via yfinance primary Global tickers, price and market cap, statements Unofficial, no SLA or key; rate limits and label drift (handled in labels.py, retry/backoff). Check Yahoo's terms before commercial use. SEC EDGAR XBRL "company facts" fallback, implemented (0.5.0) US filers only; annual 10-K figures, about five years Free, no key. SEC asks for a declared User-Agent and at most 10 requests/second. No live price, so valuation multiples are n/a from this source. Set ISOLINE_CONTACT to your email or site. Financial Modeling Prep not integrated 250 requests/day on the free plan, end-of-day; free statements limited Needs the user's own key; global coverage is paid. Candidate for an optional, key-based provider. Alpha Vantage not integrated 25 requests/day on the free key Too small for compare/screen workloads. Finnhub not integrated 60 calls/minute free, US only Standardised statements are not in the free tier. NSE/BSE filings (India) planned, unresearched Terms of use must be checked before any integration. User CSV/Excel import planned Lets users bring licensed data. Paid APIs not used Nothing is purchased by this project.

docs.title: How the fallback works
docs.text:
1. Isoline asks Yahoo Finance (three attempts with backoff).
  2. If Yahoo is rate-limited, unreachable or has no statements and the ticker looks like a plain US symbol (AAPL, BRK-B), it asks SEC EDGAR.
  3. The result carries a note naming the source ("figures come from SEC EDGAR annual filings; no live price"), and it appears in every report.
  4. Non-US tickers (INFY.NS, VOD.L) never fall back, because EDGAR does not cover them; you get the Yahoo error. Set ISOLINE_NO_FALLBACK=1 to disable the fallback.

The two sources are never blended or averaged. A line item a company did not tag stays missing.

docs.title: Not verified live
docs.text: The EDGAR provider is tested offline against a fixture built from the documented company-facts format. It could not be run against sec.gov from the development sandbox, so the first real run (for example with Yahoo blocked) is the live check.

docs.title: Growth roadmap: toward 100,000 cumulative downloads
docs.text:
Targets, not promises. PyPI download counts include CI runs, mirrors and re-installs, so they are not unique users. No bots, purchased traffic or misleading claims. Record the current number at pepy.tech/projects/isoline (and pypistats.org) before starting: that is month 0.

Milestone Target month What has to be true 15K 3 v0.4.x is the stable, easy install; first tutorials and a launch post are out 25K 5 Isoline is used in public notebooks / blog posts by people other than the author 50K 8 Listed in awesome-lists and an MCP directory; some downstream tool depends on it 75K 11 Regular contributors; second wave of features (peer valuation, DCF) shipped 100K 12 Compounding: search traffic, recommendations, CI/dependency installs

docs.title: Why people will install it (and recommend it)
docs.text:
1. It works first time. pip install isoline && isoline scan AAPL, on every OS. This release fixes the crash that hit fresh installs.
  2. It is correct and says so. Published formulas with citations and hand-computed tests (docs/methodology.md). "Shows n/a rather than guessing" is a differentiator versus scraped-ratio tools.
  3. It produces something shareable: an Excel workbook and a print-ready HTML report from one command, plus an MCP server for AI coding tools.

docs.title: Months 1-3: foundation (to 15K)
docs.text:
• Release the current version; GitHub release notes; pin the README badges; add topics: finance, piotroski, altman-z-score, beneish, stock-analysis, yfinance, mcp, cli.
  • Record a 60-second terminal GIF from a real run; add it to the README and the PyPI page.
  • Write three tutorials: "Screen for weak balance sheets with the Piotroski F-score", "Spot earnings manipulation with the Beneish M-score in Python", "Give Claude/Cursor real financial ratios with MCP". Publish on the project docs, dev.to and Medium; cross-link to the repo.
  • Post once, honestly, to r/Python, r/algotrading, r/SecurityAnalysis, r/mcp and "Show HN": what it is, what it does not do, how it is validated. Answer every comment.
  • Open "good first issue" tickets (new ratios, other data providers, tests).

docs.title: Months 4-6: distribution (to 25-50K)
docs.text:
• Submit to awesome-python, awesome-quant, awesome-mcp-servers and MCP registries/directories; Python Weekly, PyCoder's Weekly, Console.dev newsletters.
  • YouTube demo (5 min) and a short for each tutorial; ask finance-Python creators for honest feedback, not endorsements.
  • Add a Jupyter/Colab notebook so people can try it without installing.
  • Add a isoline.sdk quick example to the README (library use drives installs in other projects' requirements).

docs.title: Months 7-12: depth (to 100K)
docs.text:
• Features that earn recommendations: peer/sector valuation from a documented data source, DCF template workbook, watchlist/portfolio reports, a second data provider (reduces Yahoo dependence).
  • Conference/meetup talks (PyCon India, local Python meetups); a "How we validate financial formulas" blog post.
  • Monthly releases with changelogs; respond to issues within 48 hours.
  • Integrations: GitHub Action that posts a scan on a watchlist; pre-built MCP config snippets for each AI IDE.

docs.title: Track monthly
docs.text: Downloads (total and last 30 days, excluding mirrors where pypistats allows), GitHub stars, forks, unique contributors, open/closed issues and median response time, PRs merged, releases, docs visits (enable a privacy-friendly analytics tool if wanted), newsletter/community mentions. Review each milestone honestly; if a channel does not move numbers after two tries, drop it.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Yahoo Finance changes or blocks scraping (mitigation: second provider, clear errors); a wrong number damaging trust (mitigation: tests, citations, "not investment advice"); download counts inflated by CI (mitigation: report stars/contributors alongside downloads).

docs.title: Release process
docs.text: Status: implemented unless marked planned.

docs.title: How a release happens today
docs.text:
1. Land changes on main through normal commits (CI must be green: ruff, mypy, pytest on 3 OSes x Python 3.10-3.13, plus the clean-venv install smoke test).
  2. Bump __version__ in isoline/__init__.py (single source of truth) and add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
  3. Create a GitHub release/tag vX.Y.Z pointing at that commit.
  4. publish.yml runs:
  5. build job: tag must equal the package version; the version must not already exist on PyPI; ruff, tests, python -m build, twine check.
  6. publish job (environment pypi): uploads with Trusted Publishing (OIDC) when PYPI_API_TOKEN is unset, otherwise with that secret; then creates the GitHub release assets.
  7. smoke-test job: installs isoline==X.Y.Z from PyPI in a clean venv and runs isoline --version / --help.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
SemVer. Published versions are immutable: a bad release is fixed by publishing a new patch version (and optionally yanking the bad one on PyPI), never by overwriting or by moving/deleting tags.

Change Bump Extra gate Bug fix, docs patch none New metric/feature, backwards compatible minor none Any change to a financial formula's output at least minor must update docs/methodology.md and the hand-computed tests in the same PR; maintainer approval Breaking CLI/API change major maintainer approval

docs.title: One-time setup (needs the repository owner)
docs.text:
• On PyPI: Manage project -> Publishing -> Add a trusted publisher: owner shubhwade, repo isoline, workflow publish.yml, environment pypi.
  • On GitHub: Settings -> Environments -> pypi -> Required reviewers = yourself. This is the approval gate: nothing reaches PyPI until you click approve.
  • Never put tokens in the repo or in chat. If one is exposed, revoke it on PyPI immediately.

docs.title: Emergency release-disable switch
docs.text: Set the repository variable RELEASES_DISABLED to true (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables). The build job is skipped, so nothing is published. Set it back to false (or delete it) to resume. To stop an in-flight run, cancel it in the Actions tab or reject the pending pypi environment approval.

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text: PyPI never lets a filename be re-used. Use Yank release on PyPI for the bad version (installs of unpinned isoline skip it), then ship the fixed patch release.

docs.title: Planned (not implemented)
docs.text:
• Automatic version bump and changelog from Conventional Commits (release-please style) with a release PR. Not enabled because it would open release PRs and tags without the owner having reviewed the policy; adopt once the commit convention is in use.
  • Automated detection of "formula changed" via a golden-values test diff.
